subject: MuellerBank priority parity & rollback conditions
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: 2027-03-19T09:12:00+01:00
Subject: MuellerBank: ask for parity on priority lanes + rollback guardrails

Team — quick summary from yesterday's exec call with MuellerBank (Caroline + Tom). They're on the table for a first-year Reserved Capacity contract but their legal/security team is flagging two items that are deal blockers unless we can give clearer commitments: 

1) Priority parity: they want the same priority-lane behavior (routing, instance affinity, and warm-cache residency) that we offered to earlier strategic accounts (they called out 'HarborTrust' as the reference). Essentially they want deterministic affinity for their tenant during peak windows (08:00-20:00 CET) for the pilot period.

2) Rollback / fallback window: they need a formal rollback plan and credits if we have to failover them to a lower-tier model or different region due to capacity/compatibility within the first 90 days after go-live.

They asked for a concrete matrix and for our Product/Engineering to confirm: what we can commit today, what requires a feature work order, and an estimated timeline. They also expect an SOW-addendum for these items. I've attached the draft SOW + the parity matrix they sketched in the call (priority_parity_matrix.xlsx) and their legal's draft fallback language.

Ask: can Product/Eng sign off on a minimal set of commitments we can promise without breaking other customers or our autoscaler behaviors? If not, what is the least-friction alternative (controls, timeboxed pilot, limited hours) we can offer as a stop-gap?

Next step: Monica, can you own a one-pager for execs that lists what is product-ready vs requires roadmap work? Ben — can you scan for any infra/ops blockers (KV cache TTLs, region affinity constraints, warm-pool reservation behavior) and call out risks? Laura — can you draft the SOW addendum legal will need (we'll iterate with Caroline).

Thanks — Marcus

Attachments: mueller_sow_v1.pdf, priority_parity_matrix.xlsx

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: 2027-03-19T11:08:00+01:00
Subject: Re: MuellerBank: ask for parity on priority lanes + rollback guardrails

+1 on next steps. Quick notes from product side:

- "Priority parity" needs to be decomposed: routing (logical policy), instance affinity (node pinning for a tenant), and warm-cache (pre-warmed KV and model residency). We can commit to routing policy adjustments via configuration (no code) in 1 week for a limited-hours window.

- Instance affinity / node pinning is more complex — it intersects placement, autoscaler, and multi-tenant fairness. We can prototype a constrained pinning shim that reserves a small percentage of capacity for MuellerBank (timeboxed pilot) in ~3 sprints (6 weeks) if legal accepts limited-hours and region scoping.

- Warm-cache residency: we can offer a warm-pool reservation for their most-critical models for the pilot but it requires a short change to the warm-pool allocation algorithm (backfill behaviour). Engineering estimate below.

I'll prepare a two-column one-pager: "Safe commits (config-only)" vs "Requires roadmap/engineer work" and include estimated SLAs and fallout (e.g., cost uplift, blast radius).

Monica

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: 2027-03-20T15:32:00+01:00
Subject: Re: MuellerBank: ask for parity on priority lanes + rollback guardrails

Short engineering readout after scanning the attachments and the cluster configs:

- Routing policy (config-only): ✅ doable in <5 working days. We already support per-route preference and can introduce a tenant-priority flag that biases routing to a tagged pool. No infra change required.

- Warm-pool reservation: ⚠️ feasible but needs a small runtime change. Current warm-pool is opportunistic; reservation would require: (a) warm-pool reservation tokens surfaced to scheduler, (b) a backfill policy so we don't starve ephemeral workloads, and (c) telemetry to ensure we don't exceed SLOs. Rough estimate: 2 engineers, 3 weeks to ship a safe opt-in toggle with monitoring and rollback hooks.

- Instance pinning / node affinity: ⛔ full deterministic pinning (per-tenant on specific GPUs) is hard without hurting bin-packing. The pragmatic path: offer soft-affinity (priority scheduling to specific pools) + guaranteed quota (reserved capacity) for Reserved Capacity customers. Reserved Capacity is already our product offering; if MuellerBank is willing to accept a commit level (e.g., 40% reserved for pilot windows) we can achieve effective affinity without invasive code changes.

- Rollback/credits: We can agree contractual rollback steps (promote a fallback model, route to a different region) and compensate with a small usage credit if we initiate failover for reasons under our control. Legal will want concrete triggers (latency > X ms for Y minutes or repeated availability loss).

Risks: the warm-pool reservation introduces potential cost leakage if not paired with eviction/backfill limits. Node-affinity expectations must be calibrated — we should not promise hard pinning.

Recommendation: Offer a 6-week pilot: week 0–1 config changes + SOW addendum; weeks 2–5 warm-pool opt-in rollout; week 6 post-mortem and criteria to convert into Reserved Capacity commit. That aligns product effort and minimizes long-term technical debt.

Ben

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Caroline Mueller <caroline.mueller@muellerbank.com>
Date: 2027-03-23T16:48:00+01:00
Subject: Re: MuellerBank: ask for parity on priority lanes + rollback guardrails

Caroline / Tom — looping you in with a concrete proposal from Redwood: 

Proposal (pilot / SOW addendum):
- Configuration-only commitments (available immediately): tenant-priority routing toggle for defined pilot windows (08:00–20:00 CET), per-route latency telemetry, and a named contact for escalation.
- Engineering commitments (timeboxed pilot): warm-pool reservation opt-in (2 engineers, ~3 weeks) to ensure residency for their critical models during pilot hours. We will run this as an opt-in feature scoped to the EU region to contain blast radius.
- Affinity approach: soft affinity + reserved-capacity option. We will not promise hard node pinning; instead we offer an upgrade path to Reserved Capacity (contracted commit) that provides dedicated capacity for the pilot windows.
- Rollback / credits: if Redwood initiates a failover to a lower-tier model or different region for reasons within our control during the first 90 days post-go-live, MuellerBank will receive a 10% usage credit on affected invoice lines for the impacted week. Trigger definition: sustained p95 latency > 3x SLO for > 30 continuous minutes after remediation attempts.

Next steps: Marcus — please send this back to Caroline and Tom as an SOW addendum draft (attached). Legal: Laura will iterate on language; Monica will add the product-ready vs roadmap items to the one-pager. Ben — we'll schedule a quick 30-minute runbook review with Ops before sign.

Caroline — can you confirm whether the rollback-credit amount and the trigger definition above are acceptable? If yes, we'll move to DocuSign for the SOW addendum and target pilot start in 3 weeks.

Thanks,
Laura

Attachments: mueller_sow_v1.pdf (SOW addendum draft), prod_constraints.md (engineering summary)
